enhanced_information: In the pathophysiology of peptic ulcers, the following points are aligned with medical consensus: (opa) Much of the gastro-duodenal ulcers can indeed be attributed to H. pylori infection or mucosal injury by NSAIDs, as both are well-established causes of peptic ulcers. (opb) The statement that H. pylori is not related to the development of gastric lymphoma is false; H. pylori infection is associated with an increased risk of gastric lymphoma, specifically MALT lymphoma. (opc) The transmission of H. pylori occurs from person to person via oral-oral or fecal-oral routes, which are recognized pathways. (opd) A lower educational level and a low socioeconomic status are associated with higher rates of H. pylori colonization, likely due to factors such as crowded living conditions and poor sanitation. (ope) The incidence of gastric adenocarcinoma is higher in patients with H. pylori, as chronic infection can lead to inflammation and changes in the gastric mucosa that predispose to cancer. analysis: In the pathophysiology of peptic ulcers, Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) infection and NSAID use are well-established causes.
